A_target.statement:
Let $p \ge 1$ and $a, b \in \R^n$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \paren {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \size {a_i + b_i}^p}^{1 / p} \le \paren {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \size {a_i}^p}^{1 / p} + \paren {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \size {b_i}^p}^{1 / p}$

B_source.statement:
Let $p, q > 1$ with $\dfrac 1 p + \dfrac 1 q = 1$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \sum_i \size {x_i y_i} \le \paren {\sum_i \size {x_i}^p}^{1 / p} \paren {\sum_i \size {y_i}^q}^{1 / q}$

derived.Holder applied twice: the triangle inequality for the p-norm

object_map.reformulation: Split |a + b|^p as |a + b|^(p-1) times |a| plus |b|, and bound each piece by Hölder's inequality.

validity_conditions: The case p = 1 is the ordinary triangle inequality and must be treated separately.
The conjugate exponent satisfies (p - 1) q = p, which makes the Hölder factor a power of the same norm.
proof_plan:
For $p = 1$ the result is the [[Triangle Inequality]] summed over $i$.
Let $p > 1$ and $q = \dfrac p {p - 1}$, so $\paren {p - 1} q = p$.

By [[Hölder's Inequality for Sums]] applied to each sum:
:$\displaystyle \sum_i \size {a_i + b_i}^p \le \paren {\norm a_p + \norm b_p} \paren {\sum_i \size {a_i + b_i}^p}^{1 / q}$

If $
orm {a + b}_p 
e 0$, divide by $
orm {a + b}_p^{p / q}$.
As $p - \dfrac p q = 1$, this gives $
orm {a + b}_p \le 
orm a_p + 
orm b_p$, which is [[Minkowski's Inequality for Sums]].
{{qed}}
